Messages.Author: Wes
Messages.Body:
Pack Alpha
Combat (Common)
Animalism
A vampire may play only one Pack Alpha each round.
[ani] Employ an animal retainer from your hand before range is determined.
Pay cost as normal.
[ANI] Burn an animal retainer employed by this vampire and put this card on
this vampire. The minion with this card gets +1 strength. A minion may have
only one Pack Alpha.

----

Howler, with retained Owl Companion, gets into combat with Fatima. Fatima
shoots Owl Companion with a really big gun. Can Howler play Pack Alpha at
[ANI] after strike is declared but before Fatima's strike resolves to burn
Owl Companion and still gain the permanent effect?

Seems similar enough to Wolf Claws et al, so I am guessing the answer is
'Yes'. Traditionally, that means the answer is a resounding 'No'.

Cheers,
WES

P.S. Confidential to those who I play with: I will be abusing this card, oh
yes I will. You have been warned.

Messages.Author: Colin McGuigan
Messages.Body:
Wes wrote:
> As for the others, not exactly diverse in terms of what they do, sure. But
> being able to intercept, read your opponent's hand and do enviro-damage is
> all good in my books.

Yeah, but what do you do to avoid going to torpor yourself? I mean,
they're all great, but none of them help you avoid getting the snot beat
out of you.

And the more "keep my snot intact" cards you throw in, the less chance
you have of having the Pack Alpha+retainer combo in hand. Look at
concealed guns -- you have what, 18 cards (at least) devoted to that
combo, and that's not throwing in flash, pursuit, psyche!, etc. And
guns give you a free manuever.

The way I'm thinking is, you throw in, say, 15 masters, 20 prevent
cards, 20 wake cards, and then say 20 pack alphas and 25 retainers.

--Colin McGuigan

Messages.Author: Wes
Messages.Body:
"Colin McGuigan" <magu...@BGONEspeakeasy.net> wrote

>
> Yeah, but what do you do to avoid going to torpor yourself? I mean,
> they're all great, but none of them help you avoid getting the snot beat
> out of you.

Stay at long, or at close, whatever you need to stay alive. I think the
Ahrimanes (well, Howler) are pretty good at establishing a comfortable
distance for themselves. Swiftness of the Stag is a powerful card.

I've also added liberal doses of Guardian Angel and Leather Jacket to my
Ahrimanes decks.

> The way I'm thinking is, you throw in, say, 15 masters, 20 prevent cards,
> 20 wake cards, and then say 20 pack alphas and 25 retainers.

I don't think that many are needed.

Howler will get in combat -- we know this. So you use that opportunity to
play a retainer here and there, even if that retainer is not useful to said
combat, like Raven Spy. It basically saves you a hiring action, which is the
equivalent of Freak Drive when the cards flow right.

If anything, the problem I have had with Ahrimanes decks is not dealing with
other combat decks... but instead with *too many actions* (And PTO of
course.)

Of course, this is a new card and I have not used it yet, so don't hold me
to this jibba-jabba.

Cheers,
WES
